input.content:
Found incidentally tonight (2026-08-30) via CARD-0110 S2's base-commit test comparison, confirmed
still failing on current master directly by me: `NamedCodexAgentLaunchTests.
A_codex_agent_with_an_exact_model_id_keeps_it_and_still_sets_effort`
(tests/Antiphon.Tests/Application/NamedCodexAgentLaunchTests.cs:152).

## The failure

A Codex agent set up with `AgentModelLevel.High` and an exact pinned `ModelId = "gpt-5.6-luna"`,
started via `StartAsync`, launches with:

```
["-c", "model_reasoning_effort=high", "--model", "gpt-5.6-terra"]
```

`gpt-5.6-terra` is `ModelLevelAliases.ForCodex(High)` - the TIER alias, not the pinned
`gpt-5.6-luna` the agent was actually configured with. The test asserts `--model` should not
appear at all here ("an exact ModelId is applied by the launch resolver, not by the legacy alias
fallback").

## What this means in production

A Codex agent with an exact pinned model id launches on the WRONG model - the tier's default
instead of the one the operator explicitly chose. This is the same class of bug CARD-0138/CARD-0140
already fixed for other launch-path/profile mismatches, now apparently present for Codex
specifically.

## What's already ruled in/out (read before assuming the fix location)

`AgentTuiLaunchResolver.ApplyModelArgument` (`server/Application/Services/AgentTuiLaunchResolver.cs:462`)
itself is CORRECT in isolation - its own comment states the contract plainly ("exact wins, then a
supplied tier alias... D3 refuses an exact ModelId before we get here") and its logic at
line 469-496 does prioritize `exactModelId` over `tierAlias`. The actually-emitted `--model
gpt-5.6-terra` therefore did NOT come from this resolver - it must have come from
`AgentRegistry.Resolve` (`server/Application/Services/AgentRegistry.cs:102-125`), the
"profile-less path (pool delegates, legacy fallback)" per its own CARD-0182 D2 comment, which
computes `ModelLevelAliases.ForLaunch(kind, level)` from `options.ModelTier` alone and has NO
concept of an exact `ModelId` at all.

**The actual bug is therefore in whatever decides which of these two paths a named Codex agent's
`StartAsync` call takes** - `AgentControlService` holds an OPTIONAL `AgentTuiLaunchResolver?
launchResolver = null` (constructor at `AgentControlService.cs:61`), so there is at least one
code path that falls back to the registry directly. Find where `StartAsync` branches between
"use the launch resolver" and "fall back to AgentRegistry.Resolve", and why a Codex agent with a
pinned ModelId takes the fallback branch instead of the resolver branch that would have handled it
correctly. It's plausible this is Kind-specific (maybe Codex agents are assumed not to have a TUI
profile the resolver needs, when in fact `NamedCodexAgentLaunchTests`'s harness sets one up) or
it's a null-resolver-in-this-harness-shape issue that also reproduces in real production DI wiring
- confirm which before fixing.

## Verify

Re-run `NamedCodexAgentLaunchTests` (full class, not just the one failing test - check nothing
else in the file was relying on the current broken behavior) after the fix. The test file's other
cases presumably cover the profile-based resolver path correctly already (they pass today) - use
them as the reference for what "correct" looks like.
